andhra-pradesh.name: Pesarattu
andhra-pradesh.blurb: A thin crepe of ground whole green moong and ginger, often topped with onion and upma for a breakfast called MLA pesarattu, served with ginger chutney.

andhra-pradesh.name: Gongura Mamsam
andhra-pradesh.blurb: Mutton slow-cooked with sour gongura (sorrel) leaves and plenty of red chilli, a Guntur-style curry eaten with hot rice.

andhra-pradesh.name: Punugulu
andhra-pradesh.blurb: Crisp fried balls of leftover idli-dosa batter, sold hot from roadside carts in Vijayawada with peanut or ginger chutney.

andhra-pradesh.name: Pulihora
andhra-pradesh.blurb: Tamarind rice tempered with mustard seeds, peanuts, curry leaves and chillies, cooked at home for festivals and served as prasadam in temples.

andhra-pradesh.name: Pootharekulu
andhra-pradesh.blurb: Paper-thin rice-starch sheets layered with ghee, sugar or jaggery and nuts, a sweet from Atreyapuram in the Godavari delta.

arunachal-pradesh.name: Thukpa
arunachal-pradesh.blurb: A noodle soup with vegetables and often pork or chicken in a light broth, eaten across the Monpa and Sherdukpen areas around Tawang.

arunachal-pradesh.name: Lukter
arunachal-pradesh.blurb: Dried meat, usually pork or yak, tossed with fiery bhut jolokia chilli flakes and eaten as a side with rice.

arunachal-pradesh.name: Zan
arunachal-pradesh.blurb: A thick porridge of millet flour stirred into boiling water, sometimes with greens, a filling staple in winter villages.

arunachal-pradesh.name: Khura
arunachal-pradesh.blurb: A buckwheat pancake made by the Monpa people of Tawang and West Kameng, eaten for breakfast with chilli-cheese chutney or tea.

arunachal-pradesh.name: Khapse
arunachal-pradesh.blurb: Twisted pastries of wheat flour, sugar and butter fried crisp, made in large batches for the Losar new year.

assam.name: Masor Tenga
assam.blurb: A light, sour fish curry made with tomatoes, lemon or outenga (elephant apple), a summer favourite eaten with rice.

assam.name: Khar
assam.blurb: A dish of raw papaya or other vegetables cooked with khar, an alkaline liquid filtered from sun-dried banana-peel ash, traditionally the first course of an Assamese meal.

assam.name: Aloo Pitika
assam.blurb: Mashed potatoes mixed with raw mustard oil, chopped onion, green chilli and coriander, a simple side at almost every home meal.

assam.name: Hanhor Mangxo
assam.blurb: Duck curry cooked with ash gourd or lentils and spices, a dish closely tied to Bihu feasts and winter gatherings.

assam.name: Til Pitha
assam.blurb: Rolled rice-flour crepes filled with black sesame and jaggery, made in Assamese homes for Magh Bihu in January.

bihar.name: Litti Chokha
bihar.blurb: Wheat balls stuffed with spiced roasted gram flour (sattu), baked over coals and dipped in ghee, served with mashed roasted brinjal, tomato and potato.

bihar.name: Champaran Meat
bihar.blurb: Mutton sealed in a clay pot (handi) with whole garlic, mustard oil and spices and slow-cooked over coals, also called ahuna or handi meat.

bihar.name: Dal Pitha
bihar.blurb: Steamed rice-flour dumplings stuffed with spiced chana dal, a home-style snack popular in winter.

bihar.name: Thekua
bihar.blurb: Crisp cookies of wheat flour, jaggery and ghee pressed into wooden moulds and fried, prepared as an offering for the Chhath festival.

bihar.name: Khaja
bihar.blurb: A flaky, layered pastry fried and soaked in sugar syrup, most famous from Silao near Nalanda and Rajgir.

chhattisgarh.name: Chila
chhattisgarh.blurb: A soft pancake of rice flour batter cooked on an iron griddle, eaten for breakfast with tomato or green chutney.

chhattisgarh.name: Fara
chhattisgarh.blurb: Steamed rolls of rice-flour dough, often tempered afterwards with mustard seeds, sesame and curry leaves, a common evening snack.

chhattisgarh.name: Bafauri
chhattisgarh.blurb: Steamed dumplings of ground chana dal with onion and spices, a light, oil-free alternative to fried pakoras.

chhattisgarh.name: Chapda Chutney
chhattisgarh.blurb: A tangy chutney of red ants and their eggs ground with chilli, garlic and salt, a traditional food of the Bastar tribal region.

chhattisgarh.name: Dehrori
chhattisgarh.blurb: Fried dumplings of ground rice and curd soaked in sugar syrup, made for Diwali and weddings.

goa.name: Goan Fish Curry
goa.blurb: Kingfish or pomfret simmered in a coconut gravy soured with kokum or tamarind and red chillies, eaten daily with rice as xitt-kodi.

goa.name: Pork Vindaloo
goa.blurb: Pork marinated in palm vinegar, garlic and dried Kashmiri chillies, a Goan Catholic dish shaped by Portuguese carne de vinha d'alhos.

goa.name: Khatkhate
goa.blurb: A thick stew of several vegetables, lentils and coconut flavoured with tirphal (Sichuan-type pepper), cooked by Goan Hindu families for festivals and weddings.

goa.name: Patoleo
goa.blurb: Rice paste spread on turmeric leaves, filled with coconut and jaggery and steamed, made for the feast of the Assumption on 15 August.

goa.name: Bebinca
goa.blurb: A layered cake of coconut milk, egg yolks, sugar and ghee, each layer baked from above, served at Christmas and weddings.

gujarat.name: Khaman Dhokla
gujarat.blurb: A spongy steamed cake of fermented gram flour, tempered with mustard seeds, green chillies and curry leaves, eaten at breakfast or teatime.

gujarat.name: Undhiyu
gujarat.blurb: Winter vegetables such as surti papdi beans, purple yam and baby brinjal cooked with fenugreek dumplings, a Surat specialty eaten on Uttarayan.

gujarat.name: Thepla
gujarat.blurb: A soft flatbread of wheat flour and fresh fenugreek leaves, the standard travel food of Gujarati families, eaten with pickle or curd.

gujarat.name: Dabeli
gujarat.blurb: A pav filled with sweet-spicy potato masala, pomegranate and roasted peanuts, a street snack that started in Mandvi in Kutch.

gujarat.name: Mohanthal
gujarat.blurb: A fudge of coarse gram flour roasted in ghee with sugar, cardamom and nuts, made for Diwali and offered in Krishna temples.

haryana.name: Bajra Khichdi
haryana.blurb: Pearl millet and moong dal cooked slowly into a porridge and served with ghee, jaggery or buttermilk through the winter months.

haryana.name: Kadhi Pakora
haryana.blurb: Gram-flour fritters simmered in a sour curd-and-besan gravy, a home favourite in a state known for its dairy.

haryana.name: Hara Dhania Cholia
haryana.blurb: Fresh green chickpeas cooked with plenty of coriander leaves and spices, a seasonal winter dish.

haryana.name: Kachri ki Sabzi
haryana.blurb: A tangy curry of kachri, a small wild desert melon, cooked with onion and spices and eaten with bajra roti.

haryana.name: Churma
haryana.blurb: Crushed rotis or baked wheat dough mixed with ghee, jaggery or sugar and dry fruits, served at village festivals and weddings.

himachal-pradesh.name: Siddu
himachal-pradesh.blurb: A steamed bun of yeasted wheat dough stuffed with walnut, poppy seed or lentil paste, eaten with ghee in Kullu and Shimla villages.

himachal-pradesh.name: Chamba Madra
himachal-pradesh.blurb: Chickpeas or kidney beans slow-cooked in yoghurt with ghee and whole spices, a centrepiece of the Chamba dham feast.

himachal-pradesh.name: Chha Gosht
himachal-pradesh.blurb: Marinated lamb cooked in a gravy of yoghurt and gram flour with cardamom and bay leaf, a Kangra-region specialty.

himachal-pradesh.name: Babru
himachal-pradesh.blurb: A fried bread of wheat dough stuffed with soaked black gram paste, sold as a snack with tamarind chutney around Shimla.

himachal-pradesh.name: Mittha
himachal-pradesh.blurb: Sweet rice cooked with sugar, raisins and dry fruits, served at the end of a traditional dham meal on leaf plates.

jharkhand.name: Dhuska
jharkhand.blurb: Deep-fried bread of rice and chana dal batter, served for breakfast in Ranchi with spiced chickpea ghugni or potato curry.

jharkhand.name: Rugra
jharkhand.blurb: A curry of wild puffball mushrooms gathered from sal forests during the monsoon, cooked with onion and spices.

jharkhand.name: Chilka Roti
jharkhand.blurb: A thin pancake of rice flour and chana dal batter cooked on a griddle, a staple of tribal home kitchens.

jharkhand.name: Karil Sabzi
jharkhand.blurb: Tender bamboo shoots cooked with mustard oil, onion and chilli, a seasonal dish of the forest regions.

jharkhand.name: Arsa Pitha
jharkhand.blurb: Fried discs of rice flour and jaggery, made for festivals such as Sohrai and Karma.

karnataka.name: Bisi Bele Bath
karnataka.blurb: Rice, toor dal and vegetables cooked together with tamarind and a fresh-roasted spice powder, finished with ghee and served with boondi or papad.

karnataka.name: Mysore Masala Dosa
karnataka.blurb: A crisp dosa spread with red chutney on the inside and filled with potato palya, served with coconut chutney and sambar.

karnataka.name: Kori Rotti
karnataka.blurb: Spicy Mangalorean chicken curry in coconut milk poured over crisp, wafer-thin dried rice rotis.

karnataka.name: Coorg Pandi Curry
karnataka.blurb: Pork cooked dark and tangy with kachampuli, a vinegar made from the kodumpuli fruit, a signature dish of Kodagu eaten with rice balls (kadambuttu).

karnataka.name: Mysore Pak
karnataka.blurb: A rich sweet of gram flour cooked with generous ghee and sugar, first made in the kitchens of the Mysore Palace.

kerala.name: Onam Sadya
kerala.blurb: A vegetarian feast of rice with more than a dozen dishes such as sambar, avial, olan and thoran served on a banana leaf, especially at Onam.

kerala.name: Puttu and Kadala Curry
kerala.blurb: Steamed cylinders of rice flour layered with grated coconut, eaten for breakfast with black chickpea curry.

kerala.name: Karimeen Pollichathu
kerala.blurb: Pearl spot fish from the backwaters marinated in spices, wrapped in banana leaf and pan-roasted, a Kuttanad specialty.

kerala.name: Pazham Pori
kerala.blurb: Slices of ripe nendran banana dipped in flour batter and fried, sold at tea shops with a glass of chai.

kerala.name: Palada Payasam
kerala.blurb: Rice flakes (ada) slow-cooked in milk and sugar until pink and creamy, a classic close to a sadya.

madhya-pradesh.name: Indori Poha
madhya-pradesh.blurb: Steamed flattened rice with onion, fennel and turmeric, topped with sev and jeeravan masala, eaten for breakfast in Indore with hot jalebi.

madhya-pradesh.name: Bhutte ka Kees
madhya-pradesh.blurb: Grated fresh corn cooked in milk with green chillies and mustard seeds, a monsoon street snack at Indore's Sarafa night market.

madhya-pradesh.name: Dal Bafla
madhya-pradesh.blurb: Wheat dough balls boiled, then baked and soaked in ghee, served with spiced toor dal, a Malwa-region favourite.

madhya-pradesh.name: Bhopali Gosht Korma
madhya-pradesh.blurb: Mutton slow-cooked in a gravy of fried onions, yoghurt and whole spices, a legacy of the Nawabi kitchens of Bhopal.

madhya-pradesh.name: Mawa Bati
madhya-pradesh.blurb: Fried dumplings of khoya stuffed with dry fruits and soaked in sugar syrup, a Malwa cousin of gulab jamun.

maharashtra.name: Vada Pav
maharashtra.blurb: A spiced potato fritter in a soft pav with dry garlic chutney and fried green chilli, Mumbai's everyday street snack.

maharashtra.name: Misal Pav
maharashtra.blurb: Sprouted moth beans in a spicy, oily gravy (kat) topped with farsan, onion and lemon, served with pav, especially around Pune, Nashik and Kolhapur.

maharashtra.name: Kolhapuri Tambda Rassa
maharashtra.blurb: A fiery red mutton curry made with Kolhapuri chillies and dry coconut, served with mutton, a white broth (pandhra rassa) and bhakri.

maharashtra.name: Sabudana Khichdi
maharashtra.blurb: Soaked tapioca pearls tossed with roasted peanuts, potato, cumin and green chilli, a common food on fasting days.

maharashtra.name: Puran Poli
maharashtra.blurb: A flatbread stuffed with chana dal cooked with jaggery and cardamom, served with ghee at Holi and Gudi Padwa.

manipur.name: Eromba
manipur.blurb: Boiled vegetables such as potato and beans mashed with fermented fish (ngari) and king chilli, eaten with rice at most meals.

manipur.name: Nga Thongba
manipur.blurb: A fish curry with potatoes and onions, lightly spiced and flavoured with herbs, a regular part of the Manipuri thali.

manipur.name: Singju
manipur.blurb: A salad of shredded cabbage, lotus stem and local herbs dressed with roasted chickpea flour, chilli and usually ngari, sold at evening stalls.

manipur.name: Kelli Chana
manipur.blurb: Dried yellow peas cooked with ginger and chilli and topped with herbs, a popular street snack in Imphal.

manipur.name: Chak-hao Kheer
manipur.blurb: Manipuri black rice simmered in milk and sugar until deep purple, made for festivals and special occasions.

meghalaya.name: Jadoh
meghalaya.blurb: Red rice cooked with pork, turmeric, ginger and bay leaf, a Khasi staple sold at small eateries in Shillong.

meghalaya.name: Dohneiiong
meghalaya.blurb: Pork cooked in a thick, dark paste of roasted black sesame seeds with onion and ginger, a Khasi favourite eaten with rice.

meghalaya.name: Tungrymbai
meghalaya.blurb: Fermented soybeans cooked with black sesame, onion and chilli, often with pork, served as a pungent side dish.

meghalaya.name: Pumaloi
meghalaya.blurb: Powdered rice steamed in a special pot into soft, fluffy cakes, eaten with meat curries or tea.

meghalaya.name: Pukhlein
meghalaya.blurb: Fritters of rice flour and jaggery deep-fried until puffed and golden, a Khasi sweet made for celebrations.

mizoram.name: Bai
mizoram.blurb: A simple stew of greens, bamboo shoot and herbs boiled with a pinch of soda (chingal), the everyday Mizo dish served with rice.

mizoram.name: Sawhchiar
mizoram.blurb: Rice cooked into a thick, savoury porridge with chicken or pork, a comfort dish served at gatherings.

mizoram.name: Vawksa Rep
mizoram.blurb: Pork smoked over the kitchen fire until dry and smoky, then cooked with mustard greens or bamboo shoot.

mizoram.name: Chhum Han
mizoram.blurb: Seasonal vegetables such as cabbage, beans and pumpkin steamed and lightly seasoned, served with chilli chutney.

mizoram.name: Koat Pitha
mizoram.blurb: Fritters of rice flour, mashed banana and jaggery fried until crisp, served with tea.

nagaland.name: Smoked Pork with Bamboo Shoot
nagaland.blurb: Fire-smoked pork cooked with fermented bamboo shoot and raja mircha chilli, the dish most closely tied to Naga cooking.

nagaland.name: Axone Pork
nagaland.blurb: Pork cooked with axone, fermented soybean paste, plus tomatoes and chilli, a Sumi specialty with a strong aroma.

nagaland.name: Anishi
nagaland.blurb: Dried, fermented colocasia leaf cakes cooked with smoked pork, a traditional dish of the Ao Naga people.

nagaland.name: Hinkejvu
nagaland.blurb: A light Sumi dish of colocasia, cabbage, mustard leaves and French beans boiled together, eaten with rice.

nagaland.name: Raja Mircha Chutney
nagaland.blurb: A fiery chutney of roasted king chilli (ghost pepper), tomato and garlic, served on the side with nearly every Naga meal.
